item.title: Resource Slicing for Time-Sensitive Data Traffic in Non-Terrestrial Networks with FSO ISLs
item.description: arXiv:2610.31802v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In multi-hop Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite networks, time-sensitive packets experience queueing across multiple satellite hops, causing per-hop waiting times that accumulate and make the maximum end-to-end (E2E) delay difficult to guarantee. This paper presents a novel multi-hop slicing framework that reserves time-frequency resources for each time-sensitive flow of data originating at each satellite, aiming to maintain the reservation of communication resources along every inter-satellite link (ISL) on its route to the ground station (GS). The number of time-frequency resource blocks (RBs) reserved per-hop is determined from the data packet arrival statistics, E2E delay budget, and target level of reliability. Reservations on consecutive links are temporally aligned to enable pipelined forwarding of the time-sensitive data flows aggregated from terrestrial user terminals on the different LEO satellites. We evaluate the proposed framework against conventional scheduling and resource-allocation baselines, including pure time-division multiple access (Pure-TDMA), first-in-first-out (FIFO), and farthest-satellite-first (FSF), over the same multi-hop LEO satellite path. Under light traffic conditions, the baseline schemes provide comparable delay performance; however, their high-percentile delays increase sharply as data traffic load grows, whereas the proposed framework exhibits substantially slower delay growth. At the high arrival rate and high reliability target considered, the proposed scheme requires about 31 ms, a factor of 2.5-6.8 lower than the 76, 180, and 210 ms required by FIFO, FSF, and Pure-TDMA.
item.dc:creator: Abid Afridi, Alexis A. Dowhuszko, Risto Wichman, Jyri H\"am\"al\"ainen

item.title: Pinching Antenna Systems (PASS): Principles, Positioning and Opportunities
item.description: arXiv:2610.32068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pinching-antenna systems (PASS) have garnered significant attention owing to their ability to enhance the capacity and coverage of wireless networks by guiding electromagnetic waves through waveguides before radiation. As such, PASS are regarded as promising enabling technologies for sixth-generation (6G) communication networks. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of the state of the art in PASS, covering operating principles, positioning methodologies, performance evaluation, resource allocation, and the application of artificial intelligence (AI) to PASS-enhanced wireless networks. We first introduce the fundamental principles of PASS from both materials and physics perspectives. Building on this foundation, we present positioning methodologies for both the user side and the base station side. We then evaluate the communication performance of PASS in both uplink and downlink scenarios under different blockage models. Furthermore, we systematically review existing designs for PASS-enhanced wireless networks from a performance optimization perspective. Finally, we survey research efforts that leverage AI to address challenges in dynamic and complex scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Tianwei Hou, Yaoyu Zhang, Jinhua Wang, Guangyu Li, Zongyi Li, Minghao Jin, Anna Li, Mugen Peng

item.title: QoE-Driven Hybrid Resource Allocation for Multi-User OFDMA Semantic Communications
item.description: arXiv:2610.32077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we develop a quality-of-experience (QoE)-driven hybrid resource allocation framework for multi-user downlink orthogonal frequency-division multiple access semantic communication systems, where the hybrid framework jointly handles continuous and discrete decision variables. Specifically, we formulate a mixed continuous-discrete optimization problem to jointly optimize transmit power, subcarrier allocation, and semantic decisions under coupled power and spectrum constraints. To better characterize semantic service quality, we propose a preference-inverse multiplicative exponential QoE that is bounded and non-compensatory, capturing the intrinsic ``both-required'' property of semantic rate and similarity. To solve the optimization problem, we develop a projection-based multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient framework that enforces feasibility for continuous and discrete actions. Furthermore, we integrate Gumbel-softmax relaxation with an adaptive performance-driven temperature annealing scheme to enhance the learning of discrete semantic decisions. Simulation results demonstrate that our proposed framework achieves superior convergence, greater stability, and higher QoE compared to the conventional QoE design and penalty-based or fixed-temperature baselines, highlighting the benefits of our QoE design and the effectiveness of hybrid decision learning in semantic communications.
item.dc:creator: Xiaotian Xu, Zhifeng Tang, Guangchen Wang, Nan Yang, Xiangyun Zhou, Salman Durrani, Yansha Deng

item.title: Resilience in Wireless: A Lyapunov-Constrained Integrated Sensing, Communication, and Control Approach
item.description: arXiv:2610.32116v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional wireless networks mainly use reliability metrics to evaluate network stability. However, reliable data delivery alone cannot fully characterize network stability under variations in wireless environments and physical tasks. Wireless network resilience provides a broader perspective by describing the ability to maintain acceptable service and recover from disruptions. We develop an integrated sensing, communication, and control (ISCC) framework that incorporates communication reliability and sensing error into a state-dependent Lyapunov constraint for adaptive BS beamforming. The resulting transmit-power minimization problem is non-convex and solved via semidefinite relaxation and successive convex approximation with rank-one recovery. We establish conditional mean-square ultimate boundedness, while simulations demonstrate improved resilience and faster recovery over a static baseline.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Ge, Ningyan Guo, Yuanhao Cui, Dingyou Ma, Zhiyong Feng, Yonina C. Eldar

item.title: Type-based Over-the-Air Computation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Over-the-air computation (OAC) exploits the superposition property of wireless channels to compute functions of distributed data, reducing the communication overhead associated with its multiple access. However, existing OAC frameworks are often designed around specific classes of functions, limiting their applicability to more general nonlinear computations. This paper investigates type-based multiple access (TBMA) as a general framework for OAC, enabling the receiver to recover a histogram of the distributed observations and compute a broad class of functions without modifying the underlying communication scheme. We formulate TBMA as a histogram estimation problem and propose two digital detectors. We prove that a low-complexity successive cancellation algorithm achieves the optimal maximum-likelihood (ML) performance. We derive analytical expressions for the mean squared error (MSE) and compare TBMA with conventional schemes in terms of computation accuracy, transmission duration, bandwidth and energy consumption. Numerical experiments validate the analytical results and demonstrate that, unlike existing OAC techniques, TBMA exhibits an exponential MSE decay with increasing signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and constant transmit energy, independently of the function being computed. These findings position TBMA as a step toward more versatile OAC architectures, compatible with existing transmission schemes, and broadening the range of functions that can be computed directly over the wireless channel and enabling new possibilities for distributed computation and decision-making.
item.dc:creator: Marc Martinez-Gost, Ana P\'erez-Neira

item.title: An Evidence-Guided Framework for Tissue-Barrier Impedance Review: Deletion and Resistance Sensitivity
item.description: arXiv:2610.32579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reviewing tissue-barrier impedance requires connecting spectral anomalies with resistance estimates and experimental context. We present an evidence-guided framework that coordinates numerical checks and traceable actions for human review. In-house simulations assess the effect of removing flagged frequencies, public datasets test model adaptation, and local measurements demonstrate the review workflow. Removing flagged frequencies reduced resistance error under quadratic objectives, whereas robust fitting showed little average benefit from deletion and a mean error increase for endpoint-pair perturbations. High errors clustered around a few fitted circuit parameter sets, highlighting the value of examining parameter identifiability. Under the tested noise and perturbation conditions, these findings support robust full-spectrum estimation, flag-guided inspection, and matched sensitivity checks.
item.dc:creator: Leo Yang, Yingtong Zhou

item.title: Channel orthogonalization via movable antennas
item.description: arXiv:2610.32606v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the orthogonalization of far-field multiuser channels through the optimal positioning of the antennas constituting an array. To solve the ensuing continuous geometry optimization problem, a graph-theoretic framework is introduced that maps pairwise user channel correlations to graph edges, translating channel orthogonalization into a discrete graph-covering problem on a complete graph. The minimum number of array antennas required for orthogonalization is established for 1D, 2D, and 3D array geometries, and a binary linear program is formulated that identifies the most compact array attaining such orthogonality. The graph framework is also shown to accommodate null-steering scenarios and multipath channels. Furthermore, a fundamental tradeoff is revealed whereby relaxing exact orthogonality to near-orthogonality reduces the antenna count at the expense of a less compact array, and a method is presented to enforce minimum antenna spacings without sacrificing orthogonality.
item.dc:creator: Heedong Do, Angel Lozano

item.title: EMG Tokenization Preserves Movement Information at a Fraction of the Bitrate
item.description: arXiv:2610.32674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wireless electromyography (EMG) interfaces must balance electrode coverage against transmission bandwidth. Here, we show that compact EMG tokens substantially reduce payload while retaining information for three-dimensional hand-pose decoding. We evaluate two causal tokenizers fitted without pose labels: an encoder pretrained to reconstruct EMG spectra and one based on SPAR, an engineered spectral-spatial representation of neighbouring electrodes. In personalized, within-session experiments with 320-channel EMG from nine participants, we compare tokenized and continuous features using matched decoder architectures and training procedures. Averaged across decoders, tokenization changed mean error by +0.01 mm for SPAR (95% confidence interval: -0.12 to 0.14) and +0.45 mm for the learned representation (0.10 to 0.82). Both increases met a 1 mm non-inferiority criterion. Stored token arrays reduced payloads 41-fold relative to raw EMG and 36-fold relative to continuous SPAR features. On sampled windows of the public emg2pose benchmark's test partition, absolute differences in mean error between learned tokens and continuous features were below 0.05 mm across 176 participants and in the subset of 20 participants unseen during training. Electrode coverage, calibration, and unseen recordings affected SPAR decoding more than quantization did. In a computational benchmark, optimized SPAR generated tokens for 63 channels within 20 ms on a Cortex-M55 microcontroller. These findings support tokenization as a compact interface between wearable sensing and movement decoding, allowing decoders to be updated while the wearable encoder and transmitted representation remain fixed.
item.dc:creator: Raul C. S\^impetru, Amin Olamazadeh, Devon Rohlf, Vlad Cnejevici, Alessandro Del Vecchio

item.title: Automated Fetal Magnetocardiography Reconstruction Using a Biophysical Forward Model
item.description: arXiv:2610.32682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective: Fetal magnetocardiography (fMCG) enables early detection of cardiac disease by non-invasively measuring fetal electrophysiological activity. However, current signal estimation methods for fMCG require complex, labor-intensive human processing because they rely on blind source separation or template-based projection techniques. Methods: We propose an automated signal reconstruction approach that recovers fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG measurements without manual annotation. Our approach leverages the relationship between measurements and cardiac signals via a biophysically grounded forward model that represents cardiac sources as time-varying magnetic dipoles. This enables reconstruction of physiologically interpretable three-dimensional vectorcardiographic signals along with their spatial position. Results: Validation on synthetic data with known ground truth confirms accurate recovery of cardiac source parameters. On real fMCG recordings, the reconstruction shows strong agreement with established reference methods. Conclusion: The proposed forward-model approach automatically reconstructs fetal and maternal cardiac activity from fMCG recordings and produces signals in an interpretable vectorcardiographic source domain. Significance: Automated, interpretable fMCG reconstruction could make fetal cardiac assessment more reliable and support potential translation into prenatal care.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Emrich, Karin Narushima, Lena Wunderl, Philipp Wunderl, Tobias Jensch, Maximilian Huber, Peter Ewert, Peter Fierlinger, Annette Wacker-Gussmann, Reinhard Heckel

item.title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
item.description: arXiv:2610.32889v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, roughly half of the gain of an idealized reference.
item.dc:creator: Meizhen Zhuo, Gunter Wolff, Stephan ten Brink, Silvio Mandelli

item.title: Low-Complexity Wideband Channel Estimation for ISAC in Analog Millimeter-Wave Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.32953v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate wideband channel estimation is a key enabler for millimeter-wave (mmWave) integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. In the narrowband scenario, the Transformed Spatial Domain Channel Estimation (TSDCE) method was previously shown to provide fast and accurate angle estimation with substantially lower complexity than conventional compressed-sensing approaches based on orthogonal matching pursuit (OMP). However, wideband ISAC scenarios additionally require delay estimation, making joint angle-delay sparse recovery computationally expensive due to the multidimensional dictionary search. In this paper, we propose a wideband extension of TSDCE, namely TSDCE-TD, which incorporates time-domain support and decouples angle and delay estimation. Two variations are proposed for delay estimation: TSDCE-TD (Dict), which uses a one-dimensional delay dictionary, and TSDCE-TD (FFT), which applies Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) zero-padding interpolation. Path estimates are iteratively refined through successive interference cancellation and alternating angle-delay updates. Simulation results show that the proposed methods outperform OMP-based baselines under practical dictionary sizes, while achieving comparable performance at high-resolution settings with substantially lower computational complexity. Moreover, the angle-delay estimates obtained using the proposed approach enable accurate single-anchor indoor localization in a ray-traced environment, achieving sub-20 cm positioning errors and satisfying practical indoor positioning requirements.
item.dc:creator: Hamza Touati, Raffaele Viterbo, Mattia Brambilla, Sandra Roger, Carmen Botella-Mascarell

item.title: NECTAR: Automatic Negative Clue Estimation via Centroid-Space Mapping for Target Speaker Extraction
item.description: arXiv:2610.32133v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Target speaker extraction (TSE) aims to extract a desired speaker from a mixture using auxiliary clues such as enrollment speech. An interferer-related representation can provide a useful negative clue for TSE, but such information is not directly available from the target enrollment. To derive this representation from the observed mixture, we analyze the relationship between the speaker representations of a speech mixture and its constituent speakers. Our analysis shows that the mixture centroid lies near the midpoint of its constituent speaker centroids, whereas this relationship does not hold for single-utterance embeddings. Based on this observation, we propose NECTAR, NEgative Clue for TARget speaker extraction, which automatically derives an interferer-related negative clue from the mixture using the centroid-space relationship. We further introduce a Centroid-Space Mapper (CSM) to estimate the required centroid representations from a mixture and a target enrollment. NECTAR achieves the highest SI-SDRi on Libri2Mix among the compared systems trained on LibriSpeech train-clean-100, reaching 16.18 dB.
item.dc:creator: Hyungjun Yoo, Yongjoon Lee, Jung-Woo Choi

item.title: Incremental-Smoothing-Based ARAIM Protection Levels for Tightly Coupled GNSS/IMU Integration in Urban Canyons
item.description: arXiv:2610.32259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Protection levels (PLs) bound position errors under specified fault hypotheses and risk budgets, but advanced re-ceiver autonomous integrity monitoring (ARAIM) is formulated for snapshot GNSS estimation rather than the correlated poste-rior of tightly coupled GNSS/IMU factor graph optimization (FGO). This paper formulates ARAIM solution separation and PL computation on the FGO posterior. Because current-epoch pseudorange factors enter only the current-state block of the fixed-lag information matrix, the fault-excluded position covari-ance, solution separation, and nominal-bias propagation follow exactly from the linearized current-state marginal, which re-tains correlations with velocity, IMU-bias, and clock states and with historical information. Woodbury updates with selected-output evaluation compute these quantities for fault-free, single-satellite, constellation-wide, and second-order hypotheses with-out repeated full-state inversion or graph re-optimization. Sur-rounding monitoring layers screen measurements, handle post-fit outliers, and determine PL validity and availability. In two road experiments, both nominal sequences achieve 100% hori-zontal and vertical empirical bounding over PL-valid epochs, with a maximum error-to-PL ratio of 0.96. Normalized errors show that the posterior covariance alone does not capture slowly varying ranging biases: a covariance-only bound computed from the same posteriors retains no resolvable margin, and strong temporal correlation limits the empirical evidence to consisten-cy checks rather than validation of the integrity budget. On identical Experiment A posteriors, the proposed method reduces fault-hypothesis evaluation and PL solving time by 65.2% rela-tive to direct full-state inversion with matching integrity deci-sions, and controlled fault injections demonstrate fail-safe PL invalidation while navigation continues.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Hu (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Xiangru Wang (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Weisong Wen (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University), Meng Qian (Southeast University)

item.title: Beyond Channel Data: Configuration-Enriched Radio Foundation Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.32542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proposes incorporating channel configuration (CFG) information into Radio Foundation Model (RFM) pre-training and demonstrates that the resulting CFG-enriched embeddings serve as effective inductive priors for downstream tasks under label scarcity. We compare the proposed embeddings with raw channel tokens and multiple baseline models, under three different data regimes, for multiple downstream tasks --- Line-of-Sight/Non-Line-of-Sight (LoS/NLoS) classification, timing advance (TA) estimation, and beam selection. Evaluation is done in both in-distribution and out-of-distribution configuration settings. Experimental outcomes show that the proposed embeddings consistently outperform and/or are competitive to the baselines, across experiments in both seen and unseen configuration scenarios.
item.dc:creator: Shrihari Vasudevan, H. G. Ranjani, Raaghul Ranganathan, Satwik Sahu, Thirumaran Ekambaram

item.title: Clean-label Poisoning Attack and Defense Game for Federated Learning in Vehicular Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.32765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies interactions between clean-label poisoning attack and defense in vehicular networks using federated learning (FL). Basic Safety Message (BSM) classification for anomaly detection is modeled as a distributed learning problem over a vehicular network with dynamic topology. As a critical threat to FL, a feature-space clean-label attack is introduced, wherein benign samples are perturbed toward malicious feature extremes, degrading class separability while preserving labels. To counter this, a feature-consistency relabeling defense is proposed to detect and relabel suspicious samples. A game-theoretic framework is developed to capture attack-defense interactions and characterize equilibrium strategies based on attack effectiveness and cost parameters. Results show that the attack scales effectively with compromised nodes, while the proposed defense keeps attack success low without degrading clean accuracy and shifts equilibrium regions toward attack-averse regimes.
item.dc:creator: Yalin E. Sagduyu, Tugba Erpek, Nathan Stephenson, Mengran Xue

item.title: U-NeXt: General-purpose event detection for neonatal EEG
item.description: arXiv:2610.32811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We developed U-NeXt, a general framework for neonatal electroencephalography (EEG) event detection based on semantic segmentation. Its convolutional encoder-decoder directly segments individual channels using long input segments to preserve temporal context. A shared architecture and training framework were developed using low-voltage interval, artefact, and seizure datasets containing 51, 98, and 278 neonates, respectively, comprising over 11,000 hours of EEG and 82,000 annotated events. Performance was compared with task-specific ConvNeXt classifiers. For seizure detection, we also evaluated U-NeXt+, trained on an expanded dataset. Both U-NeXt variants and the ConvNeXt baseline were evaluated on two independent held-out seizure datasets, Helsinki and Cork, comprising 130 neonates, with recordings annotated by three experts. U-NeXt improved detection across all three event types, with particular gains in sensitivity for short events. U-NeXt+ achieved Matthews correlation coefficients of 0.862 and 0.891 on Helsinki and Cork, respectively, and improved hourly seizure burden correlations by 30-40% relative to ConvNeXt. U-NeXt+ met the criterion for expert-level performance on both datasets (p < 0.001). In separate computational benchmarks, U-NeXt reduced batch inference time relative to ConvNeXt by 254-fold on a central processing unit and 200-fold on a graphics processing unit. A common segmentation framework improves detection across diverse neonatal EEG event types while substantially reducing inference time. Accurate seizure burden estimates and performance comparable to expert reviewers support its potential use in continuous monitoring and clinical decision support.
item.dc:creator: Robert Hogan, Sean R. Mathieson, Aurel Luca, Soraia Ventura, Sean Griffin, Geraldine B. Boylan, John M. O'Toole

item.title: Multi-Timescale Context-Aware Radio Resource Optimization for Harmonious NTN-TN Coexistence: A Digital Twin and Open RAN Enabled Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.32827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coexistence between non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) and terrestrial networks (TNs) is essential for future wireless systems, but terrestrial downlink transmissions can generate harmful aggregate interference at low-Earth orbit (LEO) satellite receivers. We present DT-STABLE, an Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN)-enabled, digital twin (DT)-assisted framework for context-aware NTN-TN coexistence. Using site-specific information, the DT estimates interference at LEO satellites, enabling proactive management with reduced real-time measurement overhead. We formulate joint beam activation and user association under RF-chain limits, load balancing, and aggregate satellite interference constraints; prove NP-hardness; and develop an efficient DT-guided scheduling algorithm. DT-STABLE couples short-timescale radio resource adaptation with periodic mid- and long-timescale DT updates through standardized O-RAN interfaces. Site-specific 28 GHz simulations under worst-case satellite geometry and low elevation angles show that DT-STABLE balances rate and interference utility, achieving 89.63% interference-to-noise ratio (INR) satisfaction and a mean sum rate of 210.96 bps/Hz, with nearly 100% INR satisfaction when satellite protection is prioritized. The framework reduces beam measurement overhead by 99.71% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves up to 33.1 times lower runtime than the Gurobi-based exact optimization benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Ecem Izde Kaya, Md. Zoheb Hassan, Georges Kaddoum

item.title: SEMAC: Spherical Energy Matching Ambisonics Codec for Efficient Higher-Order Ambisonics Compression
item.description: arXiv:2610.32981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Higher-order Ambisonics (HOA) is an attractive format for immersive spatial audio, but its high channel count and directional properties present significant audio coding challenges. The widely deployed Opus audio codec supports HOA through Channel Mapping Families 2 and 3 (RFC 8486), which code and transmit every Ambisonics channel, so the bitrate grows quadratically with the spherical harmonic order. We introduce SEMAC, which instead represents an Ambisonics signal by a quantized full-order directional energy envelope together with fewer CELT-coded transport channels. CELT separates a per-band energy envelope from the signal shape and restores it after quantization, and SEMAC generalizes this principle to directional signals. Since the reduced transport spans only a lower-dimensional subspace, the decoder re-imposes the envelope observed at the encoder input, restoring the directional energy distribution at full order. A MUSHRA test on fifth-order material compares SEMAC against Opus CMF~3 in matched configurations at 512 and 768 kbit/s. SEMAC with 16 of 36 transport channels is rated above full-order CMF~3 at both rates, and at equal transport channel count above order truncation. The proposed SEMAC strategy of coding fewer transport channels with the directional envelope is found perceptually preferable to coding all HOA channels at low precision.
item.dc:creator: Christoph Hold, Jan Buethe, Jean-Marc Valin, Jan Skoglund, Toni Hirvonen, Nils Peters

item.title: Time-Varying Kernel Density Deconvolution using Random Finite Set Theory for State Noise Identification
item.description: arXiv:2412.01424v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper focuses on the noise density identification for state-space models of linear time-varying systems. The density knowledge is essential for the optimal design of any modern state estimator, fault detector, or controller. The proposed method builds on newly derived algorithms for (i) calculation of the measurement prediction residue being independent of the state and linear in state and measurement noises, and (ii) kernel density deconvolution for process with non-stationary statistical properties based on the random finite set theory. The proposed method provides consistent estimate of the state noise density without any prior knowledge on distribution family, which is a unique property in noise identification state-of-the-art. The method is further enhanced by an automatic selection of the user-defined parameters, and is evaluated in numerical examples. The examples demonstrate not only the superior performance of the proposed method in terms of accuracy and robustness among others in ultra-wide-band-inspired tracking scenario, but also the importance of the correct state noise density identification for optimal state estimation and fault detection. The paper is supplemented with a MATLAB implementation.
item.dc:creator: Jindrich Dunik, Oliver Kost, J. Krejci, Ondrej Straka

item.title: Hierarchical Coherent Imaging of Composite Anisotropic Moving Targets in ISAC
item.description: arXiv:2502.08236v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) networks, distributed devices can cooperate to produce radio images of the surrounding environment by exploiting phase-coherent signal processing. However, existing imaging methods are not well-suited for composite moving targets with multiple independently moving extended parts. This is due to simplistic isotropic scattering models and the lack of methods to compensate for distinct Doppler shifts from each component, which leads to image defocusing. We propose MOSAIC, the first hierarchical imaging method for composite moving targets using distributed User Equipments (UEs) and a single ISAC Base Station (BS). MOSAIC generates high-resolution images of each target part and estimates its velocity vector. Coherent imaging is performed within selected clusters of UEs observing a locally isotropic scattering from each part, while cluster-specific images are combined non-coherently across wide angles to improve the reconstruction. To mitigate Doppler-induced defocusing, Doppler components are pre-compensated before coherent imaging, turning a limitation into an additional means of resolving multiple target parts. This also enables low-complexity velocity estimation by associating Doppler frequencies across UEs. Simulations show a 35% to 45% improvement in image quality compared to existing methods, in terms of Wasserstein distance, and dm/s-level velocity estimation accuracy.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Pegoraro, Dario Tagliaferri, Joerg Widmer

item.title: Computationally Efficient Neural Receiver via Axial Self-Attention
item.description: arXiv:2510.12941v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Deep learning-based neural receivers offer promising physical-layer solutions for next-generation wireless systems. We propose an axial self-attention transformer neural receiver that achieves state-of-the-art Block Error Rate (BLER) performance with significantly improved computational efficiency during inference and large-scale training. By factorizing attention operations along temporal and spectral axes, the proposed architecture reduces computational complexity from $O((TF)^2)$ to $O(T^2F+TF^2)$, yielding substantially fewer floating-point operations and attention matrix multiplications per transformer block. Experimental validation under 3GPP Clustered Delay Line (CDL) channels demonstrates consistent performance gains across varying mobility scenarios. Under non-line-of-sight conditions, our proposed axial neural receiver outperforms global self-attention and convolutional neural receiver baselines at 10% BLER and 1% BLER respectively, with reduced computational complexity.
item.dc:creator: SaiKrishna Saketh Yellapragada, Atchutaram K. Kocharlakota, M\'ario Costa, Esa Ollila, Sergiy A. Vorobyov

item.title: Leaky Coaxial Cable based Generalized Pinching-Antenna Systems with Dual-Port Feeding
item.description: arXiv:2602.21856v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By leveraging the distributed leakage radiation of leaky coaxial cables (LCXs), the concept of pinching antennas can be generalized from the conventional high-frequency waveguide based architectures to cable based structures in lower-frequency scenarios. This paper investigates an LCX based generalized pinching-antenna system with dual-port feeding. By enabling bidirectional excitation along each cable, the proposed design significantly enhances spatial degrees of freedom. A comprehensive channel model is developed to characterize intra-cable attenuation, bidirectional phase progression, slot based radiation, and wireless propagation. Based on this model, both analog and hybrid beamforming frameworks are studied with the objective of maximizing the minimum achievable data rate. For analog transmission, slot activation, port selection, and power allocation are jointly optimized using matching theory, coalitional games, and bisection based power control. For hybrid transmission, zero-forcing (ZF) digital precoding is incorporated to eliminate inter-user interference, thereby simplifying slot activation and enabling closed-form optimal power allocation. Simulation results demonstrate that dual-port feeding provides notable performance gains over single-port LCX systems and fixed-antenna benchmarks, validating the effectiveness of the proposed beamforming and resource allocation designs under various transmit power levels and cable parameters.
item.dc:creator: Kaidi Wang, Zhiguo Ding, Daniel K. C. So

item.title: System Design Framework for Distributed Space Antennas Using Electromagnetic Formation Flight
item.description: arXiv:2605.23481v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Distributed space antennas using electromagnetic formation flight (EMFF) are a promising architecture for large-aperture, long-life space communication systems. Their system design, however, is governed by coupled constraints on antenna performance, satellite mass, power generation, coil geometry, and formation-keeping power. This paper proposes a system-level design framework for EMFF-based distributed space antennas. It links phased-array requirements with satellite and formation-system sizing for a static grid under a fixed total system mass. Before system-level optimization, distributed-control simulations are used to derive a control index that quantifies the formation-maintenance requirement. This index is integrated into an optimization problem with a user-defined objective and sizing, power, coil, and sidelobe-envelope constraints. Parametric case studies examine the margin magnetic moment, prescribed transmit power, and large inter-satellite spacing. Results show that increasing system mass improves footprint reduction or effective isotropic radiated power only while satellite-level design headroom remains. In direct-to-device cases with 0.15-m spacing, generated power and coil-geometry constraints dominate the feasible aperture. In the 0.30-m large-spacing case, the required coil burden can exceed satellite-level mass, size, and power capacities, making the design infeasible despite favorable communication performance. Higher-fidelity simulations of representative designs evaluate formation maintenance under nonlinear $J_2$ dynamics and antenna gain with mutual coupling, further supporting the framework's usefulness for preliminary design. The proposed framework enables the design and evaluation of feasible static grid-based EMFF distributed antennas under coupled antenna, satellite, and control constraints.
item.dc:creator: Seang Shim, Yuta Takahashi, Naoto Usami, Shin-ichiro Sakai

item.title: Task-Based Evaluation of Raw Radar Data Compression: A Pre-Registered Study of Where Classical Codecs Fail to Preserve Target Detection, and Why
item.description: arXiv:2608.17269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Synthetic aperture radar (SAR) systems collect raw I/Q echo data at rates that exceed downlink capacity; fielded systems compress onboard with block-adaptive quantization (BAQ/FDBAQ). Proposed replacements, including learned compression, are evaluated with image-quality metrics (PSNR, SSIM, SQNR); none measures whether the data still supports its operational use. We introduce a task-based evaluation methodology for raw radar compression, with a published pre-registration trail: codecs are scored after SAR focusing against a two-sided criterion -- a CFAR detection-retention floor and a spurious-detection budget at matched threshold -- using frozen task models trained once on uncompressed data. On Sentinel-1 stripmap Level-0 data the evaluation brackets the fielded FDBAQ operating point at the resolution of the BAQ grid (3-bit BAQ sustains utility at 6.12 bits per complex sample; 2-bit does not), with a reported lattice artifact found to change retention by at most 0.004. Under the final plane-mapping rule no classical configuration sustains utility below 4.86 bits per complex sample on this scene. Energy concentration after focusing delivers the predicted retention gain (0.888 vs 0.691 at 2 bits) but converts it into target-adjacent false alarms for wavelet and block-transform codecs alike: a retention-only rule certifies focused-domain JPEG2000 at 4 bits while it produces 2.5 times the tolerable spurious count. On AFRL Gotcha GMTI data (airborne, never compressed onboard) the frontier is bracketed at 7.4-8.0 bits per complex sample and the same trade reappears; on an Umbra spotlight image JPEG2000 passes the retention floor at 2, 1, and 0.5 bits while producing 10-14 times the spurious budget. We report the full pre-registration trail, including the chronology of the criterion's two clauses, one retracted overclaim, and a bounded negative result for a small learned codec.
item.dc:creator: Eric Michael Chrabot

item.title: Short-Range Microwave Interprobe Coupling in a Brain-Mimicking Phantom and Ex-Vivo Brain
item.description: arXiv:2610.16026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Objectives: Short-range wireless links (microwave range) between closely spaced devices in brain tissue are relevant to neural interfaces and intracranial sensing, yet the change in coupling between two such devices caused by a finite volume of brain-like tissue has rarely been measured directly. Technology or Method: This work characterizes a printed, microstrip-fed, parasitic-strip-loaded tapered-slot coupling probe in which only a partially inserted 12-mm wire enters the medium, while the printed structure remains outside. Results: Two fabricated probes showed a measured free-space -10-dB reflection band of 5.78 to 6.86 GHz and a fractional bandwidth of approximately 17.1%, consistent with full-wave simulation. In a controlled two-probe experiment, a homogeneous agar-gelatin-saline brain-mimicking phantom was introduced and removed while the probe arrangement and measurement conditions were retained. Introducing the phantom increased the measured transmission coefficient near 6.3 GHz by approximately 16 dB, and this differential was reproduced across repeated trials. More than five measurements in ex vivo goat brain followed the phantom transmission response within approximately 1.5 dB across the 5.78-6.86-GHz band. Time-domain analysis of the phantom-present link gave a system root-mean-square delay spread of approximately 210 ps. Full-wave dosimetry predicted a peak 1-g-averaged specific absorption rate of 1.05 W/kg for approximately 0.49 W accepted power. Conclusions and Clinical or Biological Impact: These results provide an experimentally validated reference for short-range probe coupling in brain-like media and support phantom-based bench evaluation of minimally invasive intracranial probes before in vivo studies.
item.dc:creator: Pouya Faeghi, Xiaoting Jia, Jeffrey S. Walling

item.title: On Orthogonal Recurrent Neural Networks Quantization
item.description: arXiv:2402.04012v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In recent years, Orthogonal Recurrent Neural Networks (ORNNs) have gained popularity due to their ability to manage tasks involving long-term dependencies, such as the Copy-task, and their linear complexity. However, existing ORNNs utilize full precision weights and activations, which prevents their deployment on compact devices. In this paper, we explore the quantization of the weight matrices in ORNNs, leading to Quantized approximately Orthogonal RNNs (QORNNs). The construction of such networks remained an open problem, acknowledged for its inherent instability. We propose and investigate two strategies to learn QORNN by combining quantization-aware training (QAT) and orthogonal projections. We also study post-training quantization of the activations for pure integer computation of the recurrent loop. The most efficient fully-quantized models are currently the only alternatives for solving the Copy-task with 1000 timesteps. They also surpass existing quantized models on tasks requiring long-term dependencies, such as permuted MNIST as well as some Internet of Things (IoT) tasks. However, they are less effective on tasks where long short-term memory (LSTMs) and other gated RNNs outperform ORNNs.
item.dc:creator: Armand Foucault (IMT), Franck Mamalet (Comue de Toulouse), Fran\c{c}ois Malgouyres (IMT)

item.title: Bistatic Target Detection by Exploiting Both Deterministic Pilots and Unknown Random Data Payloads
item.description: arXiv:2508.18728v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) plays a crucial role in 6G, enabling innovative applications such as drone surveillance, urban air mobility, and low-altitude logistics. However, the hybrid ISAC signal, which comprises deterministic pilot and random data payload components, poses challenges for target detection due to two reasons: 1) these two components cause coupled shifts in both the mean and variance of the received signal, and 2) the random data payloads are typically unknown to the sensing receiver in the bistatic setting. Unfortunately, these challenges could not be tackled by existing target detection algorithms. In this paper, a generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT)-based detector is derived by leveraging the known deterministic pilots and the statistical characteristics of the unknown random data payloads. Due to the analytical intractability of exact performance characterization, we perform an asymptotic analysis for the false alarm probability and detection probability of the proposed detector. The results reveal a deterministic-random trade-off: the deterministic pilots enhance detection through a target-induced mean shift, while the random data payloads provide an additional covariance-domain target signature but simultaneously introduce statistical uncertainty due to their unknown realizations. Simulations validate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed detector, which highlights the necessity of designing a dedicated detector to fully exploit the signaling resources assigned to random data payloads.
item.dc:creator: Lei Xie, Fan Liu, Shenghui Song, Shi Jin

item.title: U-STS-LLM: A Unified Spatio-Temporal Steered Large Language Model for Traffic Prediction and Imputation
item.description: arXiv:2605.11735v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Accurate spatio-temporal cellular traffic analysis is fundamental to the reliable operation of modern mobile networks, as it underpins load forecasting for congestion avoidance and missing-data imputation for continuity despite transmission errors. While deeply connected, forecasting and imputation have historically evolved as separate sub-fields. Existing models are typically task-specific, decouple temporal and spatial modeling, and rely on cascaded designs that accumulate errors and latency. Meanwhile, adapting pre-trained LLMs for this domain often leaves spatial structure under-guided and tends to overfit on limited data. To bridge these gaps, we propose U-STS-LLM, a unified framework built on a partially frozen spatio-temporally attentive (PFSTA) LLM backbone. A Dynamic Spatio-Temporal Attention Bias Generator synthesizes a persistent functional graph with transient nodal states to steer attention, while a lightweight parallel branch yields a stable local estimate fused via a Gated Adaptive Fusion, confining the LLM to residual correction. Trained under a unified multi-task objective, the model attains state-of-the-art results with low trainable-parameter overhead. Extensive experiments on real-world cellular traffic datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and transferability of U-STS-LLM, achieving average RMSE improvements of 23.7% over the strongest baselines in forecasting and 13.1% in imputation, with further gains exceeding 33% in zero-shot transfer to unseen network regions.
item.dc:creator: Yichen Zhang, Yiyang Ni, Pengcheng Xia, Jun Li, Chunguo Li
